source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.3.ANR.7: No figures: area models and number lines are described in words ("a rectangle cut into 6 equal parts, 5 shaded"; "a number line from 0 to 1 split into 8 equal parts, a point on the 5th mark"). Choice answers are LaTeX fractions, so they carry no compute; fraction numeric answers are a/b with the format stated in the stem.
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.1: No figures: shapes and lines are identified from their properties in words (square corner, equal sides, parallel, never cross). Classification of rhombus assumes the usual inclusive definitions; trapezoid and kite were avoided as options on purpose because their definitions vary.
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.2: No clock face or ruler: times are written (4:10) and lengths and capacities are given as numbers. Only customary units, no conversions between units (not in the summary).
notes.NC26.3.SGMR.3: No figures: rectangles are given by side lengths; the L-shaped area item is written as two joined rectangles with no overlap. Area by tiling is stated as squares covering a rectangle with no gaps or overlaps.
notes.NC26.3.RD.1: No graphs: scaled bar graphs and picture graphs are described in words (scale counts by 10s, each star stands for 2 books) and frequency tables are written as lists of values. The data cycle is tested through posing a collectable question and drawing a conclusion from a table.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in $4{,}732$?
questions.solution: In $4{,}732$ the 7 is in the hundreds place, so it means 7 hundreds. 7 hundreds is 700.

solve.work: 4,732: 4 thousands, 7 hundreds, 3 tens, 2 ones. The 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 700.

questions.skill: Build a number from its places
questions.stem: A number has 6 thousands, 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 9 ones. Write the number.
questions.solution: 6 thousands is 6,000. 3 hundreds is 300. 4 tens is 40. 9 ones is 9. Put them together: $6{,}000 + 300 + 40 + 9 = 6{,}349$.

questions.stem: Which number is the greatest?
questions.solution: All four numbers have 3 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 9, 9, 8 and 0. The two with 9 hundreds are 3,908 and 3,980. Compare their tens: 0 tens is less than 8 tens. So 3,980 is the greatest.

solve.work: All have 3 thousands. Compare hundreds: 8, 9, 9, 0. 3,980 vs 3,908: tens 8 > 0, so 3,980 is greatest.

questions.stem: Which choice is the number $4{,}206$ written in words?
questions.solution: $4{,}206$ is 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. That is "four thousand, two hundred six".

solve.work: 4,206 = 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones = four thousand, two hundred six.

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: regroup hundreds into thousands
questions.stem: A number is made of 3 thousands and 14 hundreds. What is the number?
questions.solution: 3 thousands is 3,000. 14 hundreds is 1,400. Together: $3{,}000 + 1{,}400 = 4{,}400$.
400 is 4 hundreds. Add 4 to the hundreds digit: 2 hundreds + 4 hundreds = 6 hundreds. The thousands, tens and ones stay the same, so the answer is 3,650.

solve.work: 3,250 + 400: add 4 hundreds to 2 hundreds = 6 hundreds, giving 3,650.

questions.stem: Which list shows $6{,}058$, $6{,}508$, $6{,}085$ and $5{,}860$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: 5,860 has only 5 thousands, so it is the least. The other three have 6 thousands. Compare their hundreds: 0, 5 and 0. So 6,508 is the greatest. For 6,058 and 6,085, both have 0 hundreds; compare tens: 5 tens is less than 8 tens. Order: 5,860; 6,058; 6,085; 6,508.

questions.skill: Add thousands, hundreds and tens in steps
questions.stem: Start at $2{,}450$. Add 3 thousands, then add 5 hundreds, then add 4 tens. What number do you reach?

questions.skill: Equivalent forms: groups of ten in a number
questions.stem: How many groups of 10 are in $3{,}460$?
questions.solution: Every 10 ones make one ten. $3{,}460$ ones is the same as 346 tens, because $346 \times 10 = 3{,}460$.

solve.work: 3,460 = 346 tens (3,460 / 10 = 346). So there are 346 groups of 10.

questions.solution: Add the ones: 5 + 4 = 9. Add the tens: 4 + 3 = 7. Add the hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. The sum is 379.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story with regrouping
questions.stem: Lena had 86 stickers. She gave 39 of them to a friend. How many stickers does Lena have now?
questions.solution: Subtract: 86 − 39. You cannot take 9 ones from 6 ones, so trade one ten for 10 ones: 16 − 9 = 7 ones. Now there are 7 tens left: 7 − 3 = 4 tens. The answer is 47. Check: 47 + 39 = 86.

questions.stem: A bakery sold 128 muffins in the morning and 145 muffins in the afternoon. How many muffins did it sell in all?
questions.solution: Add: 128 + 145. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. The total is 273.
Ones: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 8 + 1 = 15, write 5 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. The sum is 752.

questions.stem: Sam adds $364 + 258$ by adding the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones. Which choice shows his steps?
questions.solution: 364 = 300 + 60 + 4 and 258 = 200 + 50 + 8. So the hundreds are 300 + 200, the tens are 60 + 50, and the ones are 4 + 8. (500 + 110 + 12 = 622.)

solve.work: 364 = 300+60+4, 258 = 200+50+8. Hundreds 300+200, tens 60+50, ones 4+8. Only the last option has all three right.

questions.skill: Subtract in a story with regrouping twice
questions.stem: A school has 453 students. Of these, 178 ride the bus. How many students do not ride the bus?
questions.solution: Subtract: 453 − 178. Ones: trade a ten, 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: now 4 tens, so trade a hundred, 14 − 7 = 7. Hundreds: now 3 hundreds, 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 275. Check: 275 + 178 = 453.

questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as $352 + 199$?
questions.solution: 199 is 1 less than 200. Adding 200 adds one too many, so take 1 away: $352 + 200 - 1 = 551$. This is the same as $352 + 199 = 551$.

questions.skill: Find the start in a story
questions.stem: Jo had some stickers. After she gave away 148 stickers, she had 275 left. How many stickers did Jo have at the start?
questions.solution: Giving away stickers took 148 from the start. To undo it, add them back: 275 + 148 = 423. Check: 423 − 148 = 275.

questions.skill: Find a missing digit in a three-digit sum
questions.stem: A three-digit number is written 4?7, where ? is a digit that cannot be read. When 286 is added to this number, the sum is 733. What digit does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: Look at the ones: 7 + 6 = 13, so write 3 and regroup 1 ten. In the tens column, ? + 8 + 1 ten must end in 3, so ? + 9 = 13 and ? = 4. Check: 447 + 286 = 733.

solve.work: 4?7 + 286 = 733, so 4?7 = 733 - 286 = 447. Check: 447 + 286 = 733. The missing digit is 4. Only one digit works since the number is fixed by the subtraction.

questions.skill: Equal groups as a multiplication sentence
questions.stem: There are 4 bags with 6 apples in each bag. Which multiplication sentence shows the number of apples in all?
questions.solution: 4 bags with 6 apples in each bag is 4 equal groups of 6. That is $4 \times 6 = 24$ apples.

questions.stem: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, and so on. What is the 7th number you say?
questions.solution: Count by 5s seven times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. The 7th number is 35, which is $7 \times 5$.

questions.stem: A pack has 10 pencils. How many pencils are in 6 packs?
questions.solution: 6 packs of 10 pencils is $6 \times 10 = 60$. (Six tens make sixty.)

questions.skill: Match a story to a multiplication sentence
questions.stem: Which story matches $5 \times 4$?
choices: Maya has 5 pencils and then gets 4 more.
Maya has 5 pencils and then gives away 4.
Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
Maya shares 5 pencils equally among 4 friends.
questions.answer: Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
questions.solution: $5 \times 4$ means 5 equal groups of 4. 5 boxes with 4 pencils in each box matches. The other stories are adding, taking away and sharing.

solve.answer: Maya has 5 boxes. Each box has 4 pencils.
solve.work: 5 x 4 means 5 groups of 4: 5 boxes with 4 pencils each.

questions.stem: A theater has 6 rows of seats. Each row has 7 seats. How many seats are in the theater?
questions.solution: 6 rows of 7 seats is an array with $6 \times 7 = 42$ seats.

questions.skill: Break a factor apart to multiply
questions.stem: Kai finds $7 \times 8$ by breaking 7 into $5 + 2$ and writing $(5 \times 8) + (2 \times 8)$. What is $7 \times 8$?

questions.skill: Multiply by a multiple of 10 in a story
questions.stem: A box holds 30 crayons. How many crayons are in 7 boxes?
questions.solution: $7 \times 30$ is 7 groups of 3 tens. $7 \times 3 = 21$, so 21 tens, which is 210.

questions.stem: A pattern starts at 0 and adds 4 each time: 0, 4, 8, 12, and so on. Which number will be in the pattern?
questions.solution: The numbers in the pattern are what you get by counting by 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. So 36 is in the pattern ($4 \times 9 = 36$). The numbers 30, 34 and 38 are skipped.

solve.work: Pattern is multiples of 4. 36 = 4 x 9 is in it; 38, 34, 30 are not multiples of 4.

questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $6 \times 9$?
questions.solution: 9 is one less than 10, so $6 \times 9$ is 6 less than $6 \times 10$. That is $60 - 6 = 54$, and $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Share equally: size of each group
questions.stem: 12 cookies are shared equally among 4 children. How many cookies does each child get?
questions.solution: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: $12 \div 4 = 3$. Each child gets 3 cookies.

questions.skill: Make equal groups: number of groups
questions.stem: 20 stickers are put into groups of 5. How many groups are there?
questions.solution: Count how many groups of 5 fit in 20: $20 \div 5 = 4$. There are 4 groups.

questions.skill: Match a story to a division sentence
questions.stem: Which story matches $18 \div 3$?
choices: Maya has 18 pencils and gets 3 more.
18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
questions.answer: 18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
questions.solution: $18 \div 3$ means making equal shares of 18. Sharing 18 pencils equally among 3 students matches. The other stories are adding, multiplying and subtracting.

solve.answer: 18 pencils are shared equally among 3 students.
solve.work: 18 / 3 is sharing 18 equally into 3 groups. The other stories are multiplication, subtraction and addition.

questions.stem: $36 \div \square = 9$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: $36 \div \square = 9$ means $9 \times \square = 36$. Since $9 \times 4 = 36$, the box is 4.

questions.skill: Array word problem: items in each row
questions.stem: 32 chairs are put in 4 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
questions.solution: $32 \div 4 = 8$, because $4 \times 8 = 32$. Each row has 8 chairs.

questions.stem: Dan has 28 beads. He takes away 4 beads again and again until he has none left. How many times does he take away 4 beads?
questions.solution: Taking away 4 until nothing is left finds how many 4s are in 28. $28 \div 4 = 7$, so he takes away 4 beads seven times.

questions.stem: A number divided by 6 is 7. What is the number?
questions.solution: Division and multiplication undo each other. If a number split into groups of 6 gives 7 groups, then the number is $7 \times 6 = 42$.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a division story
questions.stem: 24 students are split into 4 teams with the same number of students on each team. Let $n$ be the number of students on each team. Which equation can be used to find $n$?
questions.solution: 4 teams with $n$ students each is $4 \times n$, and that equals 24 students. So $4 \times n = 24$, which gives $n = 6$.

solve.work: 4 teams of n students make 24: 4 x n = 24 (n = 6). Other equations are wrong.

questions.stem: 72 buttons are put into equal groups of 9 buttons, and $72 \div 9 = 8$. What does the 8 tell you?
choices: The number of buttons in each group
The number of buttons left over
questions.solution: Each group has 9 buttons (that is the divisor). The total is 72. The answer 8 tells how many groups of 9 can be made.

solve.work: Groups of 9 is the group size; 72 / 9 = 8 tells how many groups.

questions.stem: What is $9 \times 0$?
questions.solution: Zero groups of 9 (or 9 groups of nothing) is nothing. Any number times 0 is 0.

questions.stem: What is $18 \div 2$?
questions.solution: Splitting 18 into 2 equal parts gives 9, because $2 \times 9 = 18$.

questions.stem: What is $5 \times 7$?
questions.solution: Count by 5s seven times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So $5 \times 7 = 35$.

questions.stem: What is $7 \times 8$?
questions.solution: $7 \times 8 = 56$. One way to remember: $7 \times 8 = (7 \times 4) \times 2 = 28 \times 2 = 56$.

questions.skill: Use a multiplication fact to divide
questions.stem: Which multiplication fact can help you solve $48 \div 6$?
questions.solution: $48 \div 6$ asks: 6 times what number makes 48? The fact $6 \times 8 = 48$ answers it, so $48 \div 6 = 8$.

solve.work: 48 / 6 = ? is the same as 6 x ? = 48; 6 x 8 = 48.

questions.stem: $9 \times \square = 72$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: Ask: 9 times what makes 72? $72 \div 9 = 8$, and $9 \times 8 = 72$.

questions.stem: $6 \times 4 = 3 \times \square$. What number goes in the box?
questions.solution: $6 \times 4 = 24$. Then $3 \times \square = 24$, and $3 \times 8 = 24$. So the box is 8.

solve.work: 6 x 4 = 24 = 3 x 8, so the box is 8.

questions.stem: Pia has 42 stickers. She puts 6 stickers on each page. Let $p$ be the number of pages she fills. Which equation can she use to find $p$?
questions.solution: $p$ pages with 6 stickers on each page is $6 \times p$ stickers, and that is 42. So $6 \times p = 42$, and $p = 42 \div 6 = 7$.

solve.work: p pages with 6 each make 42: 6 x p = 42 (p = 7).

questions.stem: Which equation is true?
questions.solution: Order does not matter in multiplication: $8 \times 5 = 40$ and $5 \times 8 = 40$. But $8 \div 4 = 2$ and $4 \div 8$ is not 2; $8 \times 0 = 0$; and $8 \times 1 = 8$.

solve.work: 8 x 0 = 0 (false), 8 x 1 = 8 (false), 8 x 5 = 40 = 5 x 8 (true, commutative), 8 / 4 = 2 but 4 / 8 is not 2 (false).

questions.stem: Ben has 12 stickers. He buys 8 more stickers. Then he gives 5 stickers to his sister. How many stickers does Ben have now?
Which is the best estimate of $398 + 205$?
questions.solution: Round each number to the nearest hundred: 398 is about 400 and 205 is about 200. Then $400 + 200 = 600$. (The exact sum is 603.)

questions.stem: Mia has 3 bags with 4 apples in each bag. She eats 2 apples. How many apples are left?
questions.solution: First: $3 \times 4 = 12$ apples. Then: 12 − 2 = 10 apples.

questions.stem: A class collects cans in 6 boxes with 8 cans in each box. Then they collect 15 more cans. How many cans did the class collect in all?
questions.solution: First: $6 \times 8 = 48$ cans. Then: 48 + 15 = 63 cans.

questions.skill: Two-step: multiply then subtract from a total
questions.stem: Carlos has 50 dollars. He buys 3 notebooks that cost 7 dollars each. How many dollars does he have left?
questions.solution: The notebooks cost $3 \times 7 = 21$ dollars. Then 50 − 21 = 29 dollars are left.

questions.stem: A baker made 289 cookies on Monday and 311 cookies on Tuesday. She sold 395 cookies. About how many cookies are left?
questions.solution: Round to the nearest hundred: 289 is about 300, 311 is about 300, 395 is about 400. Cookies made: about $300 + 300 = 600$. Take away the sold ones: $600 - 400 = 200$.

questions.stem: A museum charges 8 dollars for each child and 12 dollars for each adult. A group has 5 children and 2 adults. How many dollars does the group pay in all?
questions.solution: Children: $5 \times 8 = 40$ dollars. Adults: $2 \times 12 = 24$ dollars. Together: 40 + 24 = 64 dollars.

questions.stem: Each bag has 7 red marbles and 8 blue marbles. How many marbles are in 4 bags?
questions.solution: One bag has 7 + 8 = 15 marbles. Four bags have $4 \times 15 = 60$ marbles.

questions.stem: Nina has 7 boxes with 8 beads in each box. Omar has 39 beads. How many more beads does Nina have than Omar?
questions.solution: Nina has $7 \times 8 = 56$ beads. Then 56 − 39 = 17 more beads.

questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Mia eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza did she eat?
questions.solution: The pizza has 8 equal slices, so each slice is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the pizza. Mia ate 1 slice, so she ate $\frac{1}{8}$.

solve.work: 1 of 8 equal slices is 1/8 of the pizza.

questions.skill: Numerator counts shaded parts (area model in words)
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts. 5 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: The rectangle has 6 equal parts, so each part is $\frac{1}{6}$. 5 parts are shaded, so $\frac{5}{6}$ is shaded.

questions.stem: A pie is cut into 4 equal pieces. Which fraction shows all of the pie?
questions.solution: Each piece is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the pie. All 4 pieces together are $\frac{4}{4}$, which is 1 whole pie.

solve.work: All 4 of 4 equal pieces: 4/4 = 1 whole. 4/1 would be 4 whole pies.

questions.stem: What number makes $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\square}{6}$ true?
questions.solution: Cut each half into 3 equal parts. The whole has 2 halves, which is 6 sixths. So 1 half is 3 sixths, and $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{6}$.

questions.stem: Which fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Half of 4 fourths is 2 fourths, so $\frac{3}{4}$ is more than $\frac{1}{2}$. Half of 8 eighths is 4 eighths, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$. And $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ are less than half.

questions.skill: Fraction at a point on a number line (in words)
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. A point is on the 5th mark after 0. What fraction names the point? Write your answer like 1/2.
questions.solution: Each part of the number line is $\frac{1}{8}$ long. The 5th mark after 0 is 5 of those parts from 0, so the point is at $\frac{5}{8}$.

solve.work: Each part is 1/8; the 5th mark after 0 is 5/8.

questions.stem: Which pair of fractions is equal?
questions.solution: Split each third into 2 equal parts: the whole has 6 equal parts, and 2 thirds becomes 4 sixths. So $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{6}$. In the other pairs the denominators are different but the numerators are the same, so the fractions are not equal.

questions.skill: A fraction equal to a whole number
questions.stem: Each sandwich is cut into 4 equal pieces. Lee eats 8 pieces. How many sandwiches did Lee eat?
questions.solution: 4 pieces make 1 sandwich, so $\frac{4}{4} = 1$. 8 pieces make 2 sandwiches, so $\frac{8}{4} = 2$.

solve.work: 4 pieces make one sandwich; 8 pieces = 8/4 = 2 sandwiches.

questions.stem: Which list puts $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{8}$ in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: When the top number is 1, the more parts the whole is cut into, the smaller each part is. Eighths are the smallest, then fourths, then halves. The order is $\frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}$.

solve.work: Same numerator: more parts means smaller parts. 1/8 < 1/4 < 1/2.

questions.stem: Two lines on a page never cross, no matter how far they go. What are these lines called?
questions.solution: Lines that stay the same distance apart and never cross are parallel lines. Perpendicular lines cross at a square corner, and intersecting lines cross.

solve.work: Lines in one plane that never meet are parallel lines.

questions.stem: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner (a right angle). A rectangle has 4 corners, so it has 4 right angles.

solve.work: A rectangle has 4 right angles, one at each corner.

questions.stem: An angle makes a square corner, like the corner of a book. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle that makes a square corner is a right angle.

solve.work: A square corner is a right angle.

questions.stem: An angle opens wider than a square corner, but not as wide as a straight line. What kind of angle is it?
questions.solution: An angle smaller than a square corner is acute. A square corner is a right angle. An angle wider than a square corner but not yet a straight line is obtuse.

solve.work: Wider than a right angle but less than a straight angle: obtuse.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides and no right angles. Which shape could it be?
questions.solution: A square and a rectangle both have 4 right angles, so they are out. A pentagon has 5 sides, so it is not a quadrilateral. A rhombus has 4 equal sides and does not need right angles.

solve.work: 4 equal sides: rhombus or square. Square has right angles, rectangle has right angles, pentagon has 5 sides. So rhombus.

questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: The two long sides are parallel to each other. The two short sides are parallel to each other. That makes 2 pairs.

solve.work: Opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel: 2 pairs.

questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: Every rectangle is also a square.
Every rhombus has four right angles.
Every square is also a rectangle.
Every quadrilateral has four equal sides.
questions.answer: Every square is also a rectangle.
questions.solution: A square has 4 sides and 4 right angles, so it is a special kind of rectangle. But a rectangle can have long and short sides, so not every rectangle is a square. A rhombus can lean, and any quadrilateral can have sides of different lengths.

solve.answer: Every square is also a rectangle.
solve.work: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel/equal, so it is a rectangle. The other statements are false (a non-square rhombus has no right angles, a 2-by-3 rectangle is not a square, a trapezoid need not have equal sides).

questions.stem: Lines A, B and C are all on one flat page. Line A is parallel to line B. Line C crosses line A and makes a right angle with it. What is true about line C and line B?
choices: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
Line C is parallel to line B.
Line C is the same line as line B.
Line C makes an acute angle with line B.
questions.answer: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
questions.solution: Parallel lines A and B lean the same way. If line C makes a square corner with line A, it makes a square corner with line B too. So line C is perpendicular to line B.

solve.answer: Line C is perpendicular to line B.
solve.work: C is perpendicular to A, and B is parallel to A, so C crosses B at a right angle too: C is perpendicular to B.

questions.skill: Count right angles in three shapes
questions.stem: A page has a rectangle, a square and a rhombus that is not a square. How many right angles do the three shapes have in all?
questions.solution: The rectangle has 4 right angles and the square has 4. A rhombus that is not a square has no right angles. In all: 4 + 4 + 0 = 8.

solve.work: Rectangle 4 right angles, square 4, a rhombus that is not a square has none (one right angle would force all four). 4 + 4 + 0 = 8.

questions.stem: Soccer practice starts at 4:10 and ends at 4:45. How many minutes long is practice?
questions.solution: From 4:10 to 4:45 is the same hour. Subtract the minutes: 45 − 10 = 35 minutes.

questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a watermelon?
questions.solution: Weight is measured in ounces or pounds. A watermelon is heavy, so pounds is the best unit. Inches measure length, and cups and gallons measure how much a container holds.

solve.work: Weight in customary units: pounds. Inches is length; cups and gallons are capacity.

questions.stem: A string is 12 inches long. Dina cuts off 4 inches. How many inches of string are left?
questions.solution: 12 − 4 = 8 inches are left.

questions.skill: Find an end time across the hour
questions.stem: A lesson starts at 3:40 and lasts 35 minutes. What time does the lesson end?
questions.solution: From 3:40 to 4:00 is 20 minutes. There are 35 − 20 = 15 minutes left to count. 4:00 plus 15 minutes is 4:15.

questions.stem: A bus leaves at 7:50 and arrives at 8:20. How many minutes is the bus trip?
questions.solution: From 7:50 to 8:00 is 10 minutes. From 8:00 to 8:20 is 20 minutes. In all: 10 + 20 = 30 minutes.

questions.stem: About how long is a new pencil?
questions.solution: A new pencil is a little shorter than a ruler that is 12 inches long, so about 7 inches is reasonable. 7 feet and 7 yards are taller than a person, and 70 inches is about as tall as a grown-up.

solve.work: A new pencil is about 7 inches long. 7 feet, 7 yards and 70 inches are far too long.

questions.stem: Ravi reads from 4:35 to 5:10. After a short break, he reads for 20 more minutes. How many minutes did Ravi read in all?
questions.solution: From 4:35 to 5:00 is 25 minutes. From 5:00 to 5:10 is 10 minutes. So the first reading time is 25 + 10 = 35 minutes. Then add 20 more: 35 + 20 = 55 minutes.

questions.skill: Elapsed time: find the start time
questions.stem: A dance class ended at 5:20. The class lasted 45 minutes. What time did it start?
questions.solution: Count back 45 minutes from 5:20. Going back 20 minutes reaches 5:00. There are 45 - 20 = 25 more minutes to go back, and 25 minutes before 5:00 is 4:35. Check: 4:35 plus 45 minutes is 5:20.

solve.work: Start = 5:20 - 45 min. 5:20 - 20 min = 5:00; 25 more minutes back = 4:35. Check: 4:35 + 45 min = 5:20. 4:15 is 65 min before; 6:05 adds instead of subtracts; 5:25 is after the end.

questions.stem: A fish tank had 75 gallons of water in it. Some of the water was drained, and 48 gallons were left. How many gallons of water were drained?
questions.solution: The amount drained is the part that is missing from 75. Subtract: 75 - 48 = 27. Check: 48 + 27 = 75.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 units long and 3 units wide. It is covered with squares that are 1 unit by 1 unit, with no gaps and no overlaps. How many squares cover it?
questions.solution: The squares make 3 rows with 4 squares in each row. $3 \times 4 = 12$ squares.

questions.stem: A square has sides that are each 5 inches long. What is the perimeter of the square in inches?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the distance around. A square has 4 equal sides: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 inches.

questions.skill: Area or perimeter: which to find
questions.stem: Mia wants to know how much carpet is needed to cover the floor of a rectangular room. What should she find?
questions.solution: Covering a flat surface is measured by area. Perimeter is the distance around the edge.

solve.work: Covering a floor is a question of area.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is the area of the garden in square feet?
questions.solution: Area of a rectangle = length × width. $9 \times 6 = 54$ square feet.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 centimeters long and 3 centimeters wide. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
questions.solution: A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing side of a triangle from its perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 24 inches. Two of its sides are 7 inches and 9 inches long. How many inches long is the third side?
questions.solution: The two known sides add to 7 + 9 = 16 inches. The third side is the rest of the perimeter: 24 − 16 = 8 inches.

questions.skill: Missing side of a rectangle from its perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 centimeters. It is 9 centimeters long. How many centimeters wide is it?
questions.solution: The length and width together are half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 centimeters. The width is 15 − 9 = 6 centimeters. Check: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30.

questions.skill: Area of a shape split into rectangles
questions.stem: A floor is made of two rectangles joined together with no overlap. One rectangle is 6 feet by 4 feet. The other is 3 feet by 2 feet. What is the total area of the floor in square feet?
questions.solution: First rectangle: $6 \times 4 = 24$ square feet. Second rectangle: $3 \times 2 = 6$ square feet. Total: 24 + 6 = 30 square feet.

questions.stem: Rectangle A is 6 units by 2 units. Rectangle B is 4 units by 3 units. Both have an area of 12 square units. Which statement is true?
choices: Rectangle B has the greater perimeter.
Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
The perimeters are equal because the areas are equal.
The perimeters are equal because both have four sides.
questions.answer: Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
questions.solution: Perimeter of A: 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 16 units. Perimeter of B: 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 14 units. So A has the greater perimeter, even though the areas are equal.

solve.answer: Rectangle A has the greater perimeter.
solve.work: A: 6+2+6+2 = 16. B: 4+3+4+3 = 14. A has the greater perimeter.

questions.stem: Ms. Lee's class voted for a favorite fruit. Apple got 8 votes, banana got 5 votes and grape got 7 votes. How many students voted in all?
questions.solution: Add all the votes: 8 + 5 + 7 = 20 students.

questions.skill: Read a picture graph with a key
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each star stands for 2 books. The row for Monday has 5 stars. How many books does the Monday row stand for?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 stars stands for 2 books. $5 \times 2 = 10$ books.

questions.stem: Students voted for a favorite pet. Dog got 9 votes, cat got 12 votes, fish got 4 votes and bird got 7 votes. Which pet got the most votes?
questions.solution: Compare the votes: 9, 12, 4 and 7. The greatest is 12, which is for cat.

questions.skill: Read a bar between two scale marks
questions.stem: A bar graph has a scale that counts by 10s: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40. The bar for soccer ends halfway between 20 and 30. How many students chose soccer?
questions.solution: Halfway between 20 and 30 is 25, because 10 split in half is 5 and $20 + 5 = 25$.

questions.skill: Difference using a picture graph scale
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 4 pets. The dog row has 6 pictures and the fish row has 3 pictures. How many more dogs than fish are shown?
questions.solution: The dog row has 3 more pictures than the fish row. Each picture is 4 pets, so $3 \times 4 = 12$ more dogs.

solve.work: Dogs 6 x 4 = 24, fish 3 x 4 = 12; 24 - 12 = 12 more dogs.

questions.skill: Pose a question that collects data
questions.stem: Mr. Cruz's class wants to collect data from their classmates. Which question should they ask?
choices: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
How many days are in one week?
What color is Mr. Cruz's car?
questions.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
questions.solution: A question for collecting data should have answers that can be different for different classmates. Everyone gives the same answer to the days in a week and to 7 + 5, and the car has just one color. Favorite fruit gives different answers that the class can count.

solve.answer: Which fruit do you like best: apple, banana or grape?
solve.work: A data question has answers that vary among classmates and fall into categories: favourite fruit. The others have one fixed answer.

questions.skill: Picture graph with a half symbol
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each smiley face stands for 6 students. The row for art has 3 whole smiley faces and 1 half smiley face. How many students does the art row stand for?
questions.solution: 3 whole faces: $3 \times 6 = 18$ students. A half face is half of 6, which is 3 students. Total: 18 + 3 = 21 students.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion from a frequency table
questions.stem: A class made a frequency table of how students get to school: walk 12, bus 18, car 8, bike 2. Which statement is supported by the data?
choices: More students walk than ride the bus.
Exactly half of the students ride the bus.
More students ride the bus than walk.
questions.answer: More students ride the bus than walk.
questions.solution: The bus has 18 and walking has 12, so more students ride the bus. Bike has the fewest (2). The class has 12 + 18 + 8 + 2 = 40 students, and half of 40 is 20, not 18.

solve.answer: More students ride the bus than walk.
solve.work: Bus 18 > walk 12, so more ride the bus than walk (true). Bike 2 is fewest; total 40, half is 20, bus is 18, not half.

questions.skill: Show a number of students with whole and half symbols
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each circle stands for 8 students, and half a circle stands for 4 students. 28 students chose art. Which shows the row for art?
questions.solution: Each whole circle is 8 students. 3 whole circles are 3 x 8 = 24 students, and 28 - 24 = 4 students are left. 4 students is exactly 1 half circle. So the row has 3 whole circles and 1 half circle.

solve.work: 28 / 8 = 3 remainder 4, so 3 whole circles (24) and 1 half circle (4) = 28. Others: 4 whole = 32; 7 whole = 56; 3 whole + 2 halves = 24 + 8 = 32. Only one option equals 28.
